    Supertrend

    Supertrend is a single line that trails price at a set distance. The distance is measured in ATR; the common setting is 10 periods and 3 ATR. While the line is below price the direction counts as up, while it is above as down; when a close crosses the line, it flips to the other side. The indicator describes the direction and the level at which it would change; it does not foretell the new direction.

    Which question does Supertrend answer?

    Supertrend answers this question: which way is price going now, and which level must a close cross for that direction to count as changed? The answer shows on the chart as one line. While the direction is up the line is drawn green under the candles; while it is down, red above them.

    The line moves further away or closer depending on volatility. When candles widen, ATR grows and the line moves away from price; in quiet periods ATR shrinks and the line comes closer. So the same setting works relative to the volatility of each period.

    How it is calculated

    1. Calculate ATR. The 10-period average of the candles' true range (Wilder's method). The ATR page explains it in detail.
    2. Build two bands. The candle's middle is (high + low) ÷ 2. Upper band = middle + 3 × ATR, lower band = middle − 3 × ATR.
    3. The bands only tighten. Unless the previous close crossed it, the lower band does not move down and the upper band does not move up. So the line steps along in the direction of the trend and never pulls back.
    4. Set the direction. While the direction is down, a close above the upper band turns it up; while it is up, a close below the lower band turns it down. The line is the lower band while the direction is up and the upper band while it is down.

    How it is commonly read

    • Line below price (green): since the last turn, closes have stayed above the lower band; the direction is up.
    • Line above price (red): closes have stayed below the upper band; the direction is down.
    • A turn: when a close crosses the line, the line jumps to the other side. This describes that the direction changed; it does not show that the new direction will last.
    • Distance to the line: how close price is to the line shows how much movement a change of direction would take.

    The behaviour changes with the setting. A smaller multiplier (for example 2) brings the line closer to price and turns it more often; a larger one (for example 4) turns it less often but later.

    Same line, different market

    How useful Supertrend is depends on the structure of the market.

    Clear trend

    While price moves one way, pullbacks often end before reaching the line. The line stays on the same side for a long time.

    Sideways market

    When price moves back and forth in a range, closes cross the line often; the direction turns several times at short intervals.

    One sharp candle

    A single wide candle both enlarges ATR and may cross the line. A change of direction can come from one unusual close.

    What it shows, what it does not prove

    What it shows

    • The current direction, from where recent closes sit against the bands
    • The level a close must cross for the direction to change
    • How far that level is relative to the volatility of the period

    What it does not prove

    • That the new direction will last; in a sideways market it turns often
    • The timing of a turn; the line changes with closes, so it lags
    • That a level is support or resistance; the line is a calculated distance

    The MarketLevelMap view

    How it relates to zones

    The Supertrend line is a price level, but it is not an area where the market has reacted before; it is a distance calculated from current volatility. So it should not be read as the same thing as support and resistance zones.

    Reading the two together adds context. A line sitting just below a support zone shows that, for the direction to change, price would first have to cross that zone downward as well. If the line is far from the zone, the reaction at the zone and Supertrend's direction can run independently.

    Supertrend in crypto

    Crypto trades 24/7, so ATR is not affected by session gaps, but candles narrow at weekends and at night. In those periods ATR shrinks and the line comes closer to price; a wide candle at the start of the week can then cross it more easily.

    Often confused with

    • Parabolic SARBoth draw a level that trails price. Supertrend measures the distance with ATR and turns on a close; Parabolic SAR speeds up as the trend runs on and turns when a wick reaches the level.
    • Moving averages (SMA, EMA)A moving average is the average of price and can bend either way; the Supertrend line only moves in the direction of the trend until the direction changes.

    Key points

    • Supertrend is a line trailing price 3 ATR from the candle's middle (common setting 10/3).
    • Line below and green means direction up; above and red means direction down.
    • The direction changes when a close crosses the line; this describes, it does not show that the new direction will last.
    • In sideways markets the direction turns often.
